newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican independent truckers start work stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Mexican independent truckers start work stoppage.

text.p: About 40,000 independent truck drivers in Mexico launched a work stoppage early Monday to back their demands for a wide range of better working conditions, including lower diesel prices and protection from assaults, a trucking official told Radio Red.
"We can't keep working," David Galicia, secretary general of National Confederation of Transport Drivers (CNT), said.
But he added that the truckers had not as yet set up any blockades.
"There are no blockades on the part of the confederation because this is a very serious matter," Galicia told the radio program.
Galicia told Reuters on Sunday that the drivers want a cap on diesel prices and a reduction in government red tape on obtaining licenses and permits.
On Monday, he added that the drivers want better security, given a large increase in the number of robberies.
Galicia said that the strike would last until the truckers reached an agreement with the government.
He added that they were trying to restore order in the sector, which was deregulated in 1989.
